observations.text: The resort presents overnight lodging, included water-park access and complimentary family activities as a bundled stay proposition.
Optional attraction passes, dining packages, cabanas, birthday products and other add-ons are discoverable as additional purchases layered onto the stay.

dimensions.question: How clearly does Great Wolf distinguish the base lodging-plus-water-park relationship from narrower paid attraction, dining and cabana relationships?
dimensions.reason: The base bundle and optional products are publicly distinguishable, but the clarity and prominence of those boundaries across the full discovery journey have not been systematically tested.
unanswered: The evidence does not establish whether first-time guests consistently understand what is included versus separately chargeable before beginning a booking.
Desktop and mobile ordering, prominence and comparative presentation have not been systematically inspected.

observations.text: Great Wolf operates as a pre-deposit resort, and all occupants regardless of age must be included on the reservation.
Water-park passes are included for registered guests, while attraction passes, cabanas, dining packages and other extras can create additional separately purchased commitments.
Suite occupancy and additional-person charges can affect the accommodation relationship and associated registered-guest entitlement.

All occupants must be included on the reservation, which matters because registered-guest status is tied to included water-park access.

observations.text: Registered-guest status creates the base water-park entitlement, with passes included for each registered guest.
Paid attraction passes create additional activity entitlements beyond the included water park.
Cabanas create separately reservable private-space benefits inside an environment the guest is already entitled to enter.
Meal packages create per-person, per-day dining entitlements layered onto the stay.
